tasks.short: Help employees and managers sort out contract questions and problems at work.

today.trigger: An employee or manager raises a question, disagreement or workplace problem by mail, Teams or in person.
steps: Listen to the people involved and establish what happened.
Check the employee's contract in AFAS and the applicable CAO and SharePoint policies.
Speak separately with the manager and employee where needed.
Explain the position, agree practical next steps and involve specialists for difficult cases.
Record the agreed actions in a restricted location and follow up.
drudgery: Finding the current contract and CAO clauses
Retelling the case when another HR colleague takes over
Writing follow-up notes and chasing agreed actions
today.time_sinks: Preparation and administration consume time around the conversations. Trust building, contested facts and waiting for people remain substantial parts of the task.

lenses.faster: Produce a permission-checked case brief with relevant clauses and previous agreed actions. Searching, reconstructing the chronology and drafting follow-up notes largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A new case can trigger document retrieval, missing-information checks and reminders. The system escalates conflicting clauses, sensitive allegations and disputed facts to the HRBP.
lenses.ambitious: Give every shift and site a timely response and check whether agreed remedies actually worked. Use recurring, aggregated problems to improve working arrangements before they become disputes.
lenses.joy: Remove copying, searching and chasing. Keep the conversations in which the HRBP restores trust and helps people reach a workable agreement.
lenses.options: Prepare several possible resolutions with their contractual constraints and likely effects. The HRBP tests these with the people involved.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP sets case-handling standards and fixes recurring causes instead of rebuilding every case from scratch.
reach: Prepare routine employee-service responses currently handled by HR Administrators.
Give the HR Director an anonymised view of recurring employee-relations issues.

tasks.human_edge: Employees need a trusted person who notices power imbalances, hears what is left unsaid and takes responsibility for a fair resolution.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: evidence retrieval and drafting are checkable, but mediation, disputed facts and sensitive employment judgments require a person to lead.

in_practice.trigger: The HRBP opens a restricted case and requests a preparation brief.
steps: Retrieve only documents the HRBP is entitled to access, including the applicable contract and effective CAO version.
Draft a chronology that separates reported claims, confirmed facts and missing information.
Show relevant clauses with source links and flag conflicts or uncertainty.
After the conversation, draft an action note from information the HRBP chooses to provide.
Save the approved note and schedule agreed follow-ups.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP verifies the facts and interpretation, conducts the conversations and approves all advice, commitments and case notes.
systems: AFAS Profit through an authorised integration
data_needed: Contract, employment status and applicable CAO
Current policies with effective dates
Relevant correspondence and approved case notes
Access rights, retention rules and escalation criteria
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint case record, recording sources, draft version, reviewer and agreed actions; technical logs exclude unnecessary case content.

evidence.claim: SharePoint supports document versioning and access controls that can underpin a controlled case library.
Retrieval and drafting can reduce case preparation, provided the HRBP checks facts and contractual interpretation.
The 35% human-time saving and 1.3 times end-to-end speedup are unvalidated planning estimates; conversations and response delays remain.

risks: Applying the transport CAO to an employee covered by the warehouse CAO, or using an outdated clause.
Disclosing confidential allegations or personal information through overly broad retrieval permissions.
Turning one party's account into an apparently established fact.
Recording medical diagnoses in an HR case; absence cases need only information HR may lawfully process.
research_questions: What proportion of case time goes into preparation and administration versus conversations and waiting?
Can AFAS and SharePoint access rights reliably restrict retrieval to the assigned HRBP?
Does a pilot preserve factual accuracy, employee trust and resolution quality while reducing preparation time?

tasks.short: Explain which HR rules apply and what employees and managers need to do.

today.trigger: An employee or manager asks about leave, working hours, allowances, absence procedures or another HR rule.
steps: Clarify the question and identify the employee group and applicable CAO.
Find the relevant policy, contract clause or legal guidance.
Check effective dates, exceptions and previous interpretations.
Explain the answer in plain language and describe the next action.
Refer uncertain or consequential cases to the relevant specialist.
drudgery: Answering the same policy questions repeatedly
Searching across policy files and mail threads
Rewriting formal wording into practical instructions
today.time_sinks: Routine questions are quick individually but arrive throughout the day. Exceptions require checking several sources and consulting Payroll or the HR Director.

lenses.faster: Answer approved routine questions directly from current sources, showing the relevant clause and next action. Repeated searches and rewriting disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A question triggers an answer only when the applicable policy and employee group are clear. Missing sources, conflicting rules and consequential interpretations go to HR.
lenses.ambitious: Make reliable policy help available outside office hours for warehouse and transport shifts. Offer reviewed translations and check understanding for common procedures.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive explanations of straightforward rules. Keep the nuanced advice and improvements to policies that employees find confusing.
lenses.options: Offer a short answer, a worked example and a manager checklist from the same approved rule. Compare lawful routes where a policy explicitly allows alternatives.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP owns the quality and coverage of the policy-answer service, including its exceptions and source updates.
reach: Absorb routine policy questions from HR Administrators.
Prepare general payroll-policy explanations for the Payroll Specialist to approve.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP resolves ambiguous interpretations, explains difficult outcomes sensitively and recognises when a routine question conceals a larger problem.
tasks.pattern_why: Llm_step: the model translates a question and approved source material into a cited explanation inside a rules-based workflow. Only bounded routine answers qualify for automatic delivery.

in_practice.trigger: An authenticated employee or manager submits a question through a shift-accessible HR help channel.
steps: Establish the relevant employee group using the minimum necessary identity and employment data.
Retrieve approved sources with effective dates and a defined order of precedence.
Draft a plain-language answer with citations and an explicit next action.
Apply checks for unsupported statements, conflicting sources and excluded topics.
Deliver an eligible routine answer or route the complete question and sources to HR.
Record feedback and suspend affected answers when a source changes.
in_practice.human_gate: HR and relevant specialists approve sources and answer boundaries before launch. Individual disputes, legal uncertainty, contract changes and Wet verbetering poortwachter case advice require human review.
systems: AFAS Profit through a limited authorised lookup
Teams or an authenticated mobile-accessible HR channel
data_needed: Approved policies, both CAOs and reviewed legal guidance
Effective dates, policy owners and source precedence
Minimal employee-group attributes
Escalation topics and tested reference questions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted HR answer log with question category, cited source versions, routing outcome and feedback; identifiable content follows a defined retention schedule.

evidence.claim: SharePoint provides versioned libraries and permissions for maintaining approved policy sources.
A retrieval workflow can draft cited answers and route exceptions, but legal correctness requires source governance and testing.
The 60% human-time saving and 2.2 times end-to-end speedup assume a substantial routine-question share and working access for shift employees.

risks: A fluent answer conceals a missing exception or incorrect interpretation.
Employees receive different answers because CAO coverage or effective dates are wrong.
Warehouse employees cannot access the channel without a company account or suitable device.
Personal questions expose unnecessary employee data; apply AVG/GDPR purpose limitation and access controls.
Scope expands into employment decisions, requiring a fresh EU AI Act classification and assessment.
research_questions: What share of recent questions can be answered from a single approved rule without interpretation?
Can the service pass a reference set covering both CAOs, exceptions and policy changes?
Can all shifts access it, and do employees understand the answer and escalation route?
Who will own source updates and withdraw incorrect answers immediately?

tasks.short: Help site managers match available people and skills to staffing needs.

today.trigger: A site faces a staffing gap, seasonal peak, changed workload or proposed internal move.
steps: Collect staffing needs, available capacity and current flex orders from the three sites.
Check contracts, working-hour constraints and required certificates.
Discuss employee preferences and operational needs with site managers.
Compare overtime, flex workers, training and internal moves.
Agree a proposal with managers and coordinate approved changes.
drudgery: Combining differently formatted staffing lists
Checking certificate status person by person
Recalculating options after each manager change
today.time_sinks: Collecting current availability and reconciling site assumptions dominate preparation. Agreement with managers and employees determines the final timetable.

lenses.faster: Combine staffing needs, availability and certificate checks into one validated planning view. Repeated spreadsheet merging and recalculation disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Updated demand or a certificate expiry triggers a gap alert and refreshed scenarios. The system prepares options without assigning employees or ordering flex workers.
lenses.ambitious: Plan skills coverage across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo before peaks arrive. Identify where training or predictable contracts would reduce repeated flex dependence.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet reconciliation and repeated eligibility checks. Keep the negotiations that balance service, fairness and employee preferences.
lenses.options: Compare overtime, agency cover, voluntary transfers and training under the same cost and safety constraints. Show infeasible options and why they fail.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP defines staffing constraints and improves workforce planning with operations instead of manually assembling each proposal.
reach: Prepare workforce-cost scenarios with FP&A.
Identify certificate and training gaps for Learning and Development.
Prepare flex demand forecasts for agency coordinators.

tasks.human_edge: Managers and the HRBP judge fairness, suitability and operational realities that availability tables do not capture, while employees have a voice in proposed moves.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic_software: capacity arithmetic, certificate validity and explicit staffing constraints belong in checkable code or an optimiser. People approve assignments and resolve exceptions.

in_practice.trigger: A site manager submits a demand change or an agreed planning cycle starts.
steps: Import current demand, availability, contract constraints, certificate validity and agency capacity.
Flag missing or stale inputs and block scenarios that cannot be verified.
Calculate staffing gaps and feasible alternatives using explicit constraints.
Show cost, skills coverage, travel requirements and preference conflicts for each scenario.
Let the HRBP and site managers select and adjust a proposal.
Send approved actions to the responsible scheduler, administrator or agency coordinator.
in_practice.human_gate: Site managers retain operational assignment authority. The HRBP checks employment constraints and fairness, employees are consulted where needed, and material policy changes follow applicable OR procedures.
systems: Excel or a custom rules-based planning service
data_needed: Site demand and actual availability from the scheduling source
Contract hours and relevant CAO constraints
Certificate type, validity and operational authorisation
Agency capacity and agreed rates
Employee preferences and agreed travel constraints
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted staffing-planning record with input timestamps, constraint versions, scenarios, approvers and final changes.

evidence.claim: Excel Solver can optimise a numeric objective subject to explicit constraints.
A rules-based planning service can combine validated availability and certificate data without a language model.
The 40% human-time saving and 1.4 times end-to-end speedup depend on timely availability data and leave consultation time intact.

risks: The listed systems do not establish a reliable source for live rosters and availability.
A valid certificate is mistaken for full operational competence or site authorisation.
An optimiser repeatedly burdens the same employees or ignores travel and personal constraints.
Medical diagnoses enter staffing inputs; use only necessary, lawfully available work-capacity information.
If AI materially informs individual assignments, assess EU AI Act employment-use requirements; human approval alone does not settle classification.
research_questions: Where are actual rosters, availability and demand maintained, and how current are they?
Can the model reproduce a recent staffing plan while satisfying CAO, safety and preference constraints?
Do managers and employees accept the proposed trade-offs across sites?
Can this remain rules-based, or would the intended individual recommendations bring additional AI and OR obligations?

tasks.short: Help managers improve hiring and keep new starters productive and here after 90 days.

today.trigger: A manager reports hard-to-fill vacancies, rejected offers or early departures, or a workforce review identifies a problem.
steps: Review Recruitee funnel data and AFAS hiring and departure records.
Check onboarding completion, training and available evidence of productivity.
Speak with managers, Recruiters and recent starters about likely causes.
Develop recruiting or retention options with costs and responsibilities.
Agree a pilot and review results with the manager.
drudgery: Joining candidate records to employee records
Rebuilding site and job-group comparisons
Preparing similar programme briefs for each manager
today.time_sinks: Data reconciliation and agreeing what productive at day 90 means slow analysis. Learning whether an intervention works still requires elapsed time.

lenses.faster: Prepare a joined funnel and day-90 briefing with missing-data warnings. Manual exports, cohort comparisons and first-draft programme documents largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled review detects aggregate changes in offer acceptance, week-one onboarding and 90-day retention. It prepares a briefing for the HRBP and Recruiter.
lenses.ambitious: Run measured improvements for each site and major job group, tied to productive hires who stay for 90 days. Compare interventions over several cohorts instead of relying on anecdotes.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated dashboard preparation and document assembly. Keep diagnosis with managers and designing changes that improve the new starter experience.
lenses.options: Compare realistic packages such as better shift previews, buddy cover, faster offers and protected onboarding time. Show expected cost, uncertainty and the evidence needed to choose.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP manages a portfolio of hiring and retention experiments with clear owners and outcomes.
reach: Prepare funnel diagnostics with the Recruiters.
Develop intervention business cases with FP&A.
Coordinate onboarding improvements with Learning and Development.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP understands site culture, challenges weak explanations and secures manager commitment to changes that affect daily work.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: software can assemble evidence and draft options, but causal diagnosis, programme choices and organisational commitment stay with the HRBP.

in_practice.trigger: A monthly cohort review or a manager request starts a programme assessment.
steps: Build validated joins between Recruitee, AFAS and Studytube using agreed identifiers.
Calculate funnel and retention measures for cohorts with a complete observation window.
Combine aggregate findings with approved qualitative feedback and show data limitations.
Draft several intervention briefs with costs, owners and measurable hypotheses.
Have the HRBP, Recruiter and manager choose a pilot and success criteria.
Track implementation and report results with uncertainty and relevant operational changes.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP and manager approve interventions and employee-facing changes. Relevant specialists and the OR are involved where required; the service does not rank candidates or predict individual departures.
data_needed: Vacancy dates, pipeline stages and offer outcomes
Start dates, employment status and departure dates
Week-one onboarding and training completion
An agreed operational measure of productivity
Programme costs, implementation dates and cohort definitions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint programme register with metric definitions, source snapshots, approved hypotheses, pilot decisions and measured outcomes.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports data modelling and scheduled refresh for recurring cohort reporting.
Joined cohort analysis and structured intervention briefs can improve preparation, but observed associations do not establish causes.
The 40% human-time saving and 1.5 times speedup apply to preparing advice, not to shortening the 90-day outcome window.

risks: Using retention alone as a substitute for the North Star's productivity requirement.
Comparing incomplete 90-day cohorts with fully observed cohorts.
Attributing seasonal, pay or manager effects to an intervention without sufficient evidence.
Small groups reveal individuals or invite unfair comparisons between sites.
Expansion into AI candidate ranking or individual retention scoring may trigger EU AI Act high-risk employment requirements and additional AVG/GDPR duties.
research_questions: Can candidate and employee records be joined accurately, and is productivity recorded consistently?
Are cohort sizes large enough to distinguish useful changes from seasonal variation?
Which interventions can managers implement consistently and compare credibly?
Does a pilot reduce preparation time and improve decisions without introducing individual scoring?

tasks.short: Coach managers to interview fairly, discuss performance and document problems properly.

today.trigger: A manager needs help before an interview, appraisal or difficult performance conversation, or a training session is due.
steps: Clarify the manager's situation and review relevant policy or documentation.
Find suitable interview questions, conversation guidance and recording templates.
Adapt examples to warehouse, transport or office work.
Coach the manager or deliver training and practise difficult moments.
Review proposed documentation and agree follow-up support.
drudgery: Adapting the same training materials repeatedly
Finding examples and templates
Correcting vague or judgmental wording in drafts
today.time_sinks: Material preparation and individual draft reviews take time. Building a manager's confidence and judgment requires practice and feedback.

lenses.faster: Draft a role-specific coaching pack from approved material and flag unclear documentation. Repeated slide preparation and template adaptation disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A manager's request or training assignment generates a practice pack and reminders. The system tracks completion through Studytube where integration permits.
lenses.ambitious: Offer short practice sessions to every shift manager before important conversations. Check whether managers can apply the guidance, beyond completing a course.
lenses.joy: Remove slide production and repetitive wording corrections. Keep coaching managers through situations where better listening and judgment matter.
lenses.options: Generate several fair interview questions and conversation openings, with examples of useful factual documentation. Let managers rehearse different employee responses using fictional cases.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP designs and checks a manager-development system rather than preparing each coaching session from the beginning.
reach: Co-design manager learning modules with Learning and Development.
Prepare structured interview guides with the Recruiters.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP recognises avoidance, bias and poor management habits, gives candid feedback and judges whether a sensitive case needs direct support.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: drafting and fictional practice can be automated, but coaching quality and advice on consequential employee cases require professional judgment.

in_practice.trigger: A manager requests support or enrols in an approved management module.
steps: Select approved material for the topic, role and applicable policy.
Generate a short guide, checklist and fictional practice scenario.
Allow text-based rehearsal without uploading identifiable employee cases.
Flag discriminatory questions, unsupported judgments and missing factual details in drafts.
Have the HRBP review sensitive material and coach the manager.
Record learning completion and agreed follow-up without retaining unnecessary practice transcripts.
in_practice.human_gate: HRBP and Learning and Development approve reusable content. HR reviews real performance-case documentation and any advice that could support an employment sanction.
data_needed: Reviewed interview and performance-management guidance
Role requirements and fictional logistics scenarios
Documentation standards and escalation rules
Training assignments and completion status
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube for completion and restricted SharePoint for approved materials and coaching actions; practice transcripts are not retained by default.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can help draft presentations from supplied content.
Language models can generate fictional role-play and alternative wording, with reviewed guidance needed for employment topics.
The 45% human-time saving and 1.6 times end-to-end speedup assume reusable approved materials and substantial preparation work.

risks: Training normalises biased interview questions or weak performance-management practices.
A polished document makes unsupported allegations look well established.
Managers put confidential employee details into an unapproved service.
Course completion is mistaken for competence.
Voice or video practice is used to infer workplace emotions; keep rehearsal text-based and avoid emotion recognition.
research_questions: How much HRBP time goes into reusable material preparation versus live coaching?
Do managers using the practice pack demonstrate better interviewing and documentation in assessed fictional cases?
Can content owners keep guidance current and catch discriminatory or legally weak suggestions?
Can shift managers access short practice sessions during paid working time?

tasks.short: Design safe ways for employees to report concerns and say what needs improving.

today.trigger: HR reviews employee listening arrangements, introduces a policy or sees signs that complaints are not reaching the right people.
steps: Review existing surveys, complaints and participation across sites and shifts.
Consult employees, site managers and the OR about barriers and trusted channels.
Draft questions, reporting routes and rules for confidentiality and follow-up.
Check privacy, accessibility and responsibilities with relevant advisers.
Pilot the approach and revise it before wider use.
drudgery: Rewriting questionnaires and process documents
Comparing overlapping question sets
Manually checking whether each site and shift can participate
today.time_sinks: Design and document preparation can be shortened. Trust, OR consultation and testing confidentiality arrangements require deliberate human work.

lenses.faster: Draft question sets, channel maps and follow-up procedures from an agreed brief. Repetitive document preparation and coverage checks disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Approved surveys can launch on a schedule and trigger response-rate checks and agreed reminders. Named complaints follow a separate restricted route with a responsible person.
lenses.ambitious: Hear from every site and shift, including flex workers through clearly agreed agency arrangements. Close the feedback loop so employees can see what changed.
lenses.joy: Remove questionnaire formatting and administrative monitoring. Keep the work of earning trust and helping employees influence their working conditions.
lenses.options: Compare anonymous pulses, facilitated discussions and confidential named reporting. Make the trade-offs in access, follow-up and identification risk explicit.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP owns the employee-listening and complaint-handling design, checking participation, safety and whether issues lead to action.
reach: Define survey and reporting requirements with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Prepare employee consultation materials for the HR Director and OR.

tasks.human_edge: Employees decide whether a channel feels safe. The HRBP must earn that trust, protect complainants and respond responsibly to serious concerns.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: AI can draft and compare methods, but choosing confidentiality arrangements, consulting the OR and designing trustworthy complaint handling remain human responsibilities.

in_practice.trigger: An approved review of employee-listening or complaint procedures begins.
steps: Map audiences, shift access, existing channels and known participation gaps.
Draft alternative methods and check question clarity, accessibility and identification risks.
Agree confidentiality, aggregation, retention and serious-complaint routing with responsible advisers.
Consult the OR and complete applicable approval steps before implementation.
Pilot across office and shift populations and test whether employees understand each channel.
Launch the approved approach and monitor participation and action follow-through.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves the design with the HR Director and privacy adviser, and obtains OR consent where legally required. A trained person handles identifiable complaints and safeguarding concerns.
systems: Microsoft Forms configured for the approved identity settings
Approved enterprise language-model service for design drafts
data_needed: Site and shift population counts
Existing listening methods and participation statistics
Approved question bank and employee-language needs
Confidentiality, retention and escalation rules
Agency agreements for flex-worker participation
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint design and consultation record; named complaints remain in a separate restricted register from survey responses.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Forms supports surveys, branching and configurable respondent-name recording.
AI can draft questionnaire alternatives, but technical settings alone cannot guarantee anonymity or employee trust.
The 35% human-time saving and 1.2 times end-to-end speedup assume less drafting work while consultation and piloting remain.

risks: Calling a survey anonymous when metadata, free text or small groups can identify respondents.
Routing an urgent harassment or safety complaint into a periodic survey with no timely response.
Introducing complaint or personnel-data arrangements without applicable OR consent under the WOR.
Survey fatigue grows because managers do not act or explain their decisions.
Flex workers lack safe access or fear their agency will see individual responses.
research_questions: Which groups currently do not participate, and what prevents them from speaking?
Do employees correctly understand the difference between anonymous feedback and confidential named complaints?
Can the pilot meet the agreed privacy protections and route serious concerns promptly?
Who owns follow-up, and can managers demonstrate that feedback led to visible action?

tasks.short: Turn employee feedback into clear reports and presentations for managers.

today.trigger: A survey closes or management requests an employee-satisfaction update.
steps: Export survey results and approved aggregate complaint statistics.
Clean responses and check participation by site and employee group.
Calculate results, compare periods and summarise free-text themes.
Build charts and a presentation with limitations and proposed actions.
Review sensitive findings and present them to management.
drudgery: Cleaning the same survey exports each cycle
Rebuilding charts and copying figures into slides
Reading repetitive comments and checking that totals match
today.time_sinks: Data preparation and presentation assembly dominate production. Sensitive findings and management discussion still need the HRBP.

lenses.faster: Use fixed calculations and charts, then draft a source-linked narrative from approved aggregate results. Cleaning, chart rebuilding and slide copying largely disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Survey closure triggers validation, privacy checks and a draft report. A person approves the narrative and audience before release.
lenses.ambitious: Provide consistent reports for all three sites and track whether agreed improvements changed later responses. Include participation and uncertainty alongside scores.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet and slide production. Keep interpreting the findings with managers and agreeing practical changes.
lenses.options: Create an executive brief, a site-manager discussion pack and an employee update from the same validated figures. Compare plausible interpretations without presenting them as proven causes.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP sets reporting standards and challenges management's response instead of assembling each reporting pack.
reach: Take on recurring employee-feedback reporting from the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Prepare approved employee and OR feedback summaries for the HR Director.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP judges whether a summary fairly represents employees, challenges defensive interpretations and handles difficult management conversations.
tasks.pattern_why: Agent_with_gate: deterministic software validates and aggregates figures, while an LLM step drafts themes and narrative. The HRBP approves interpretation and disclosure before the report counts.

in_practice.trigger: An approved survey closes or a scheduled reporting deadline arrives.
steps: Import responses and run fixed completeness, duplicate and participation checks.
Calculate approved metrics and suppress small groups, including combinations that could reveal suppressed values.
Redact identifying free text before drafting themes and flag uncertain classifications.
Generate charts, a draft narrative and presentation from the validated reporting dataset.
Have the HRBP verify figures, themes, disclosure risk and proposed actions.
Publish the approved audience-specific pack and archive its source snapshot.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves every report's narrative and disclosure before distribution. Serious allegations in comments go to a restricted human review route rather than into presentation material.
systems: Excel or a deterministic data-processing service
data_needed: Survey responses and survey-version metadata
Eligible population counts and reporting periods
Approved metric definitions and comparison rules
Minimum group-size and disclosure-control rules
Approved aggregate action and complaint statistics
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted reporting audit record with dataset version, calculation results, suppression rules, draft themes, reviewer changes and publication audience.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports repeatable data transformations, reports and scheduled refresh.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI and Power Query

evidence.claim: A model can draft feedback themes and narrative, but minority views, allegations and identifying details require review.
The 70% human-time saving and 2.5 times end-to-end speedup assume stable survey definitions, reusable templates and a prompt approval cycle.

risks: A generated narrative contradicts the figures or invents a cause.
Theme summaries obscure minority concerns or the seriousness of a single allegation.
Small groups, direct quotations or comparisons identify respondents.
Changing questions or response patterns makes period comparisons misleading.
A draft reaches managers before privacy and interpretation checks are complete.
research_questions: Can fixed calculations reproduce the last approved report exactly?
Do human reviewers agree that generated themes preserve minority and serious concerns?
Can disclosure testing prevent identification through quotes, filters and overlapping groups?
How much production time remains once review, corrections and presentation are included?

role.altitude: The HRBP becomes the owner of reliable people processes and manager capability across the three sites: setting rules, reviewing exceptions and turning recurring problems into improvements.
reach: Routine policy-service design and quality checks with HR Administration.
Recruitment-funnel and day-90 programme analysis with the Recruiters.
Manager learning design and certificate-gap planning with Learning and Development.
Aggregate employee-feedback reporting with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst.
Workforce and intervention cost scenarios with FP&A.
Preparation of consultation evidence and recurring-issue briefings for the HR Director and OR.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks cover 798.4 hours per HRBP annually, about half of the stated role time. The proposed human-time savings total about 361.6 hours per HRBP, or 1,085 hours across three FTE, worth about EUR 86,800 in capacity at EUR 80/hour. This is an unvalidated planning estimate, not a cash saving; integration upkeep, source review, overlap between tasks and extra improvement work reduce the recoverable hours. No estimate is made for the remaining role tasks. Trust, mediation, legal accountability, manager adoption, OR consultation and the time needed to observe 90-day outcomes limit further automation.
skills_to_grow: Maintain CAO and policy sources with clear ownership, effective dates and escalation rules.
Test AI answers and summaries against reference cases and inspect exceptions.
Define productivity, cohort measures and credible intervention comparisons.
Apply AVG/GDPR data minimisation, confidentiality and reporting disclosure controls.
Recognise employment uses that need EU AI Act assessment and applicable OR involvement.
Specify rules-based workforce scenarios and challenge their assumptions.
Coach managers and lead sensitive conversations with evidence and empathy.
role.ambitious_version: Run a joined hire-to-day-90 improvement programme across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Give shift employees reliable policy help, managers practical coaching, and each site a measured plan for onboarding, skills coverage and retention. Use the released capacity to improve the share of open roles filled by people who become productive and remain after 90 days, while tracking absence, manager satisfaction and fair treatment.
